passages:
Generic conformances own their telescopes independently of data declarations.
Select one through a nested application with every type, const,
and static-machine argument explicit; expected shape or visibility cannot infer
them. Lifetime elision is application-only, under the rule below. Proof-only
and runtime-capable implementations use the same conformance model. Their
requirements determine execution and erasure; absence of a data subject is
universal and does not exclude an implementation from dynamic selection.

An inline member is an ordinary machine with its own identity and supplies
one exact requirement overload. When inherited names or overloads collide,
its signature and ordinary exact `satisfies Trait<...>::member` edge identify
the requirement; ambiguity rejects rather than selecting by visibility.
Member implementations refine the requirement's complete
[machine contract](machines.md#substitution), not merely its value signature.
A forwarding body must meet those same proof, ownership and operational
obligations. Forwarding does not equate the member with its callee, donate the
callee's establishment authority, or erase trust dependencies. Optimizations
may eliminate a call or share physical code only while preserving these
semantic identities and contracts; correctness never depends on that optimization.

Constants are not fields and do not contribute to `size_of<T>()`. Their complete
types recursively permit copying and have no cleanup obligation, shared
ownership, or interior mutability. Fixed arrays, records, and copy-eligible sums
are eligible; selecting an unrestricted active case does not make a structurally
linear sum eligible. A constant has no stable address and grants no authority.

A constant position requests semantic evaluation. An initializer may call an
ordinary machine only when that concrete invocation is admitted for evaluation;
there is no separate `const machine` species. The evaluator's admission contract
is described in [semantic evaluation](evaluation.md#invocation-admission).
Effectful [build execution](../build/execution.md) is a separate operation.

passages:
Normal returns owe applicable postconditions for both value and Unit results.
An implicit return occurs after the executable portion's final statement, not
after executing trailing declarations. A selected returning arm uses that arm's
facts. A terminal call owes both the callee's result and the caller's completion
contract; lexical ancestry adds no further return targets. Crash edges are not
normal returns. Synthetic `result` denotes the exact returned value; output-reference
parameters retain their actual reference origins.

Exit proof consumes live facts, not the conclusion being proved. Reference-subject
transport across calls or loop edges does not transport the truth of an expired
entry assumption. Declaration contexts cannot receive a sibling invocation's facts.
Outcome-specific guarantees follow the matching nominal result case and remain
separate from unconditional guarantees, as specified in
[proof availability](../proofs/contracts.md#identity-availability-and-erasure).

`dropped by` selects one exact independent static cleanup machine for an owned
qualified occurrence. It names the operation the compiler invokes at cleanup,
not a list of callers permitted to discard the value. It takes one machine
application, with generic arguments supplied from the declaration's binders:

One selected operation must satisfy all applicable domain, custody and loan
obligations, including inherited ones. Zero selected operations permits ordinary
structural cleanup only where disposal is otherwise legal; it does not discharge
an unresolved linear claim. Selection does not itself prove the hook's
preconditions or give it read/write or issuance authority. The owning package's
selection is the explicit authorization of that cleanup plan; a linear terminal
disposition still must account for every obligation under the ownership rules.

Moves and intact transport preserve the selection and its obligations. Alias
expansion, predicate weakening and explicit qualification erasure cannot remove
cleanup debt or evade a selection conflict. Borrowing does not authorize disposal
of the referent. Cleanup selection belongs to the owned qualified subject, not
to an ambient collection of predicates the compiler happens to prove. Normalized
machine identity and substituted arguments are part of the domain's semantic
interface. No hidden runtime domain tag is introduced.
